I will still do it the way I usually decide on my land: start from what worked before, then adjust a little for cost and water. I have 16.9 mu, so this is not a tiny plot anymore. I cannot manage it like a kitchen garden, but I also cannot throw money around. Cotton takes more watching, more spraying, and more picking work, but if I feed it too lightly and it sets fewer bolls, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. Maize is steadier and easier to manage, so I will use it to balance labor and cash. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will not put all 16.9 mu into the crop that needs the most hands at the busiest time. I will split the land with more cotton and some maize, keep using well irrigation, and stay close to what farmers around me do here in Hebei.

For cotton, I will use improved seed, plough once before planting, then make a fine seedbed. I will not cut fertilizer too hard. I will put enough base fertilizer so the plants start strong, then topdress nitrogen when growth picks up. Cotton on our side is afraid of weak growth early and also afraid of too much rain at the wrong time, so with well water in hand I will irrigate at key times instead of waiting for the sky. I will spray more often on cotton because aphids, bollworm, and other problems can come one after another. For maize, I will keep it simpler. I will use hybrid seed, rotary tillage, a solid base fertilizer, then one more nitrogen feeding later. Maize must not go hungry around jointing and filling, so I will keep fertilizer there even if fertilizer prices are not cheap. If the season is normal, this plan will give me a harvest I can count on without pushing costs too far.
